Messages.Author: Bindusara
Messages.Body:
I should know this but it keeps coming up in our games...

If i'm being bled and i deflect the bleed to another Meth (and don't
declare a block) then the bleed gets deflected back to me, have I
forgone my chance to block? I haven't decided not to make any further
attempts to block. When do I actually declare this?

thanks all for clarification,

jds

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
"Bindusara" <bind...@my-deja.com> wrote in message
news:90j6d0$ahd$1...@nnrp1.deja.com...

> I should know this but it keeps coming up in our games...
>
> If i'm being bled and i deflect the bleed to another Meth (and don't
> declare a block) then the bleed gets deflected back to me, have I
> forgone my chance to block?

Not necessarily. When the acting Methuselah declares the bleed you may
deflect it immediately OR you may decline to block and then deflect it. The
latter is usually done in an attempt to trick the acting Methuselah into
adding a bleed increasing modifier before you deflect the bleed.

> I haven't decided not to make any further
> attempts to block. When do I actually declare this?

If you don't decline to block you may make a block attempt if the bleed is
bounced back to you.

-Robert

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
"Halcyan 2" <halc...@aol.com> wrote in message
news:20001205184433...@ng-mi1.aol.com...


No. Once you decline to block you cannot change your mind just because the
bleed is deflected back to you. The decision not to block is final. If you
want to reserve the option to block, you should deflect the bleed before
choosing to block or not block the action.

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
<theve...@my-deja.com> wrote in message news:90juni$pp$1...@nnrp1.deja.com...

> Can you agree to take a bleed but then when they add a modifier on
> decide to block or does the agreeing to take the bleed imply that you
> declined to block?

You can agree to take the bleed (which is akin to saying "I decline to
block"). That's how I'd rule a dispute if it came up during a tournament.
Whenever someone responds to "So and So bleeds for 1" with "I'll take it" or
"give me the total" that is meant to be a declination of blocks. This *has*
come up before though. A smart player will demand that other methuselahs
respond with official terms.

Player A: "Roreca bleeds for 1."
Player B: "OK, what's the total?"
Player A: "So, you are declining to block?"

That's the way to clarify it. It is theoretically possible that player B is
just trying to ascertain whether player A has a laptop on her, etc. Its
best to get people to use game terms to avoid misunderstandings.

--

> should deflect the bleed before choosing to block or not block the

Actually, yes.

Changing the target of an action results in a new "choose blockers"
opportunity. [RTR 30-JUN-1997] This was explicit in the Jyhad
version of Deflection, but has since been moved to the realm of
"rulings".

A need for this ruling can be seen in the following scenario:
Alex, Bela, and Cleo are seated in that order around the table.
Alex controls Anneke, Bela controls Brachah, and Cleo controls
Cameron.

Brachah bleeds Cleo. Cleo declines to block and Alex declines to
block with Anneke. Brachah plays Aire of Elation to make the bleed
+2. Cameron plays Deflection to make Brachah bleed Alex.

Alex can now have Anneke attempt to block the action.

Similarly with the bounce-back situation described above.
